subject.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)

question: Should OpenClaw permanently expose an opt-in `turnMaintenanceTaskTimeoutMs` setting and process-wide abort ownership for deferred context-engine maintenance, or should this failure mode be handled by an existing host safety/recovery policy instead?
rationale: The implementation is designed to avoid silently changing existing users' timeout behavior, but that makes a reported interactive-session availability failure remain unbounded by default; choosing the permanent default, configuration surface, and shutdown ownership is product and lifecycle policy rather than a mechanical defect fix.

options.title: Sponsor the opt-in contract
options.body: Accept the new setting and lifecycle fence as the supported operator-controlled mitigation, with the current default preserving existing behavior.

options.title: Use a host-owned bounded policy
options.body: Replace the new configuration surface with a maintainer-selected host safety/recovery timeout that has explicit upgrade and plugin-contract proof.

options.title: Defer the direction
options.body: Keep this PR open but pause merge until the agent/session owners define the canonical timeout and shutdown contract.

recommendation.title: Use a host-owned bounded policy
recommendation.body: Replace the new configuration surface with a maintainer-selected host safety/recovery timeout that has explicit upgrade and plugin-contract proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The branch author is the strongest available routing contact for the proposed implementation, while the final API and lifecycle direction still requires an owning maintainer decision.
